title: Protein Only Diet Effects
hook: What if you ate only protein?

beats.line: Blood sugar falls, causing mental fog.
beats.idea: Character’s eyes glaze, thought bubbles swirl.

beats.line: Urine calcium rises, increasing kidney stone risk.
beats.idea: Kidney cartoon pumps urine streams, bladder bulges.

beats.line: Kidneys churn extra urea, urine flow spikes.
beats.idea: Cracked lips and a parched skin close‑up.

beats.line: Mouth dries, skin tightens, thirst hits hard.
beats.idea: Skeleton glows, calcium particles drift away.

beats.line: Gut slows, stool piles up, belly feels bloated.
beats.idea: Colon fills, character holds a rounded belly.

description: A quick look at how an all‑protein diet stresses your body over weeks.

facts.claim: High protein intake increases urea production, adding extra load to kidneys.
facts.source: NIH, National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

facts.claim: Low carbohydrate intake can cause low blood glucose and mental fog.
Excess protein raises water loss, leading to dehydration.
Acidic byproducts of protein metabolism can cause calcium loss from bones.
facts.source: NIH, Acid–base balance and bone health

facts.claim: Lack of dietary fiber leads to constipation.

end.line: Could you survive on protein alone?

topic: What happens if you eat only protein?
